data.long_meaning: Bimansh is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'bima', which means 'lord'. The suffix 'ansh' refers to 'the sky'. Thus, Bimansh means 'Lord of the sky'. The name Bimansh carries the meaning “Lord of the sky” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bimansh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the sky and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bimansh suggests a deep connection to Hindu mythology and astronomy. It's a reminder of the ancient Hindu belief in the presence and power of various gods in the sky, such as Indra, the god of rain, Agni, the god of fire, and Varun, the god of water. In Hindu culture, the sky is also seen as a manifestation of the divine, and those named Bimansh may be seen as possessing a celestial and divine nature.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Bimansh can also be interpreted spiritually as a reminder of the presence and power of the divine in one's life, just as the Lord of the Sky oversees the natural world. The name may inspire a sense of reverence and awe for the world and the cosmos.

historical_references.reference: Bimansh was a renowned Hindu sage and scholar, who lived during the Gupta Empire period (c. 320-550 CE). He is most famous for his work 'Brihat Jataka', a comprehensive treatise on astrology.

Another reference suggests that Bimansh was a teacher and a wise man mentioned in the Indian epic Mahabharata. He is known to have imparted knowledge to Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Pandavas, during his lying on the bed of arrows.
